This paper examines the extent of how AI-assisted decision-making improves operational effectiveness without undermining human command and ethical responsibility. Focusing on United States military applications of AI in intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance, and defensive systems, the analysis evaluates both performance gains (speed, consistency, and data fusion) and risks. Applying an ethical framework grounded in human-in-the-loop principles and Just War Theory, this paper identifies key failure modes such as automation bias. The findings argue that while AI systems can meaningfully enhance tactical effectiveness, their unbounded use risks weakening the human judgment necessary for lawful and morally accountable military action.
